findings.title: Radar is visually broken
findings.problem: The radar is a dark disc with faint green crosshairs and a tiny triangle, but no visible sweep line, no clear blips, and no range rings. It reads as a broken placeholder rather than a functional instrument.
findings.why: Players look to the radar for immediate spatial awareness. A radar that looks dead undermines trust in the UI and gives no useful information about threats or terrain.
findings.fix: Add a bright rotating sweep arc in a high-contrast green, visible concentric range rings in faint lines, and replace the tiny player triangle with a brighter, slightly larger arrow. Enemies should appear as bright red or yellow dots that stand out against the dark background.

findings.title: City scene is a monochromatic wash
findings.problem: The ground, buildings, road, and walls are all the same muted grey-blue tone with almost no value or hue contrast between them. The entire scene flattens into a single texture with no visual hierarchy.
findings.why: Players cannot quickly distinguish buildings from ground from paths. The scene feels unfinished and lifeless, making it hard to navigate or identify points of interest.
findings.fix: Darken the ground by 20-30% in value and shift it slightly warm (brown-grey). Raise the buildings by 10-15% in value with a cooler tint to make them pop forward. Add a subtle warm highlight or rim light on building tops facing the implied sun direction. Keep the road a mid-value neutral that separates ground from structures.

findings.title: Highway lane markings are disconnected dashes
findings.where: Road screen (center, the two yellow lane markers)
findings.problem: The lane markings are rendered as separate short yellow rectangles with gaps between them, but the gaps are as wide as the marks themselves, making them look like floating debris rather than a painted road.
findings.why: At speed, players need the road to read instantly as a road. Broken lane markings reduce the sense of forward motion and make the highway feel like a flat grey plane with random tokens on it.
findings.fix: Render the lane markings as continuous or at least longer dashes with narrow gaps (standard highway ratio is about 10ft mark, 30ft gap). Add a faint white shoulder line along both road edges to frame the drivable surface and give peripheral speed cues.

findings.title: Status panel is information-dense with no scan path
findings.where: Arena screen and Road screen (right sidebar, full height)
findings.problem: The right panel stacks ARMOUR, TYRES, and PLANT & DRIVER in three separate boxes with small green text and tiny bar fills. Every number looks the same weight and color, so nothing stands out. Critical info (zero body armor in red) is buried at the bottom.
findings.why: In a fast combat scenario, players need to glance at their status and instantly know what is damaged. The current panel requires reading line-by-line, which is too slow. The equal visual weight of all fields means nothing has priority.
findings.fix: Reduce the panel to two rows: a vehicle silhouette showing armor per side as a color-coded outline (green/yellow/red), and a compact row of tyre icons. Move the critical zero-body-armor warning to a persistent red flash in the center-bottom HUD, not buried in a sidebar.

findings.title: Title screen shows tanks, not cars
findings.problem: The background artwork depicts two military tanks with turret-mounted cannons facing each other. The game is described as a car-building courier combat RPG, and all gameplay screenshots show a small civilian-style car.
findings.why: The title screen sets player expectations. Tanks suggest a military simulator or war game, not a scrappy car-building highway survival game. This mismatch creates immediate cognitive dissonance and may attract the wrong audience while repelling the right one.
findings.fix: Replace the two tanks with two heavily modified, armored cars or trucks facing off in the same dramatic composition. Keep the sunset city silhouette and cracked road — those fit the tone. Show a car that matches the in-game vehicle class (subcompact with welded armor plates, mounted guns) to accurately represent the gameplay loop.
